title: A Harbor for the Vow
premise: Marine biologist Lior Pemberton inherits a third of a failing coastal orchard alongside two strangers: Juniper Vale, a sharp-tongued archivist, and Elias Thorne, the estranged brother of Lior's late first love. The deed's fine print binds all three to live on and restore the land for one year or lose it to a predatory developer. As storms, sabotage, and old secrets test them, Lior must choose between protecting his heart and telling the truth about the night his love died. In the end, he confesses, forgives himself, and lets Juniper stay after the last train leaves—claiming both the orchard and a future.
about_author: Mirabel Yarrow is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set where the land meets the sea. She lives in a converted boathouse with an opinionated heron she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Deed That Wouldn't Die
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A lawyer delivers news of an inheritance tied to an orchard Lior has avoided for seven years—the place where his first love, Wren Thorne, died. He arrives intending to sign away his share but finds two other claimants already arguing on the porch. Emotional beat: dread sharpened into reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Three Names, One Fence
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper, an archivist who traced the deed through decades of forged signatures, lays out its cruel clause: one year of shared residency or the developer buys it outright. Elias, Wren's brother, wants to sell immediately; Lior says nothing about knowing him. Emotional beat: uneasy alliance formed over mutual stubbornness.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior throws himself into surveying the orchard's neglected creek, counting turtle nests as a way to avoid people. Juniper follows, asks inconvenient questions, and catches him flinching at Wren's name. Emotional beat: the first crack in his armor—annoyance that feels dangerously like interest.

chapters.title: What Elias Buried
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias reveals he returned not for the orchard but for answers; Wren's letters stopped abruptly before her death. He finds Lior's name in her last letter and confronts him. Lior lies. Emotional beat: guilt metastasizing, loyalty to the dead curdling into deception.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A storm floods the low orchard; the three work through the night sandbagging the creek and save the oldest trees. Soaked and laughing afterward, Lior and Juniper share a near-kiss interrupted by Elias watching from the window. Emotional beat: warmth arriving exactly when it's most dangerous.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The developer offers each claimant a personal buyout—enough to erase debts—if they turn on the others. Lior discovers someone already signed. Suspicion poisons the household just as the turtles hatch. Emotional beat: trust fracturing under the weight of money and old wounds.

chapters.title: Letters in the Root Cellar
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Juniper uncovers a tin of Wren's unsent letters proving her death was an accident—and that she'd planned to reconcile with Elias and confess something to Lior. Juniper realizes Lior has been carrying false blame. Emotional beat: tenderness turning protective; truth becoming unavoidable.

chapters.title: The Night I Didn't Save Her
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Cornered by Elias and the deed's deadline, Lior finally tells the whole story: the argument, the storm, the seconds too slow. Grief breaks open between the brothers. Emotional beat: climax—confession as both devastation and release.

chapters.title: Last Train Out
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias, forgiven and forgiving, chooses to stay and rebuild rather than sell, signing the final papers at dawn. But Juniper, hurt that Lior let her defend a lie, packs for the last train. Emotional beat: victory hollowed out by the cost of silence.

chapters.title: A Harbor for the Vow
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. At the station, Lior doesn't beg—he simply tells the truth again, this time forward-facing, and offers her the choice to stay. She misses the train on purpose. One year later, the orchard blooms, the turtles nest, and three names share one deed willingly. Emotional beat: resolution—love chosen in full daylight.
